claims.text: High-entropy alloy nanoparticles contain five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios.
Rapidly quenched, equiatomic multi-metal nanoparticles can initially form a well-mixed single-phase solid solution.
Severe lattice distortion raises local energetic barriers for atomic diffusion.
Higher diffusion barriers suppress the atomic movement that produces phase segregation or chemical ordering at elevated temperatures.
Severe lattice distortion preserves a metastable single-phase solid solution over 473–1923 K.
Single-solid-solution HEA nanoparticles can retain similar structures from 573 to 1000 K.
The cited evidence establishes structural and chemical stability across the full 473–1923 K range.
Reduced lattice distortion enhances atomic diffusion.
Nanoparticles with lower lattice distortion will exhibit more phase separation than nanoparticles with higher distortion.
Selecting constituent metals with substantially different atomic radii increases lattice distortion.
Selecting constituent metals with similar atomic radii produces comparatively low lattice distortion.
Deviations in interatomic bond lengths and the distribution of local strain can quantify lattice distortion.
Rapid quenching combined with atomistic simulations can produce nanoparticles with controlled degrees of lattice distortion.
Configurational entropy can lower the free energy of simple HEA solid-solution phases at high temperatures and make ordered intermetallic compounds less competitive.
Mechanical stress, oxidation, and deviations from equiatomic composition can affect nanoparticle structural or chemical stability.
Surface segregation may alter the proposed distortion–diffusion relationship at the nanoscale.

contradictions.description: The design claims that only intrinsic lattice distortion is varied, but the high- and low-distortion sets use different constituent elements. Changing elemental identities also changes chemistry, mixing thermodynamics, surface energies, and diffusion kinetics, so the comparison does not isolate lattice distortion.
